items.headline: Centre introduces bill to raise women's minimum age of marriage to 21 years
items.text: The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 was introduced in the Lok Sabha to raise the minimum marriageable age of women from 18 to 21 years, overriding personal laws, and was referred to a Parliamentary Standing Committee.

items.headline: Parliament passes Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021 enabling Aadhaar-voter ID linkage
items.text: With the Rajya Sabha's approval amid an Opposition walkout, Parliament passed the Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021, which allows electoral registration officers to seek Aadhaar details for voter verification, provides four qualifying dates a year for enrolment and makes service-voter provisions gender neutral.
items.why: Raised privacy concerns and was later challenged in the Supreme Court.

items.headline: Mediation Bill, 2021 introduced in Rajya Sabha, referred to Standing Committee
items.text: The Mediation Bill, 2021 was introduced in the Rajya Sabha, proposing mandatory pre-litigation mediation for civil and commercial disputes, enforceable mediated settlement agreements, online mediation and a Mediation Council of India. It was referred to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Law and Justice.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes NDPS (Amendment) Bill, 2021 to correct drafting error in Section 27A
items.text: The Lok Sabha passed the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Bill, 2021 to correct a drafting error in Section 27A (punishment for financing illicit traffic and harbouring offenders), which cross-referred to a clause that had been renumbered by an earlier amendment. The Bill replaced an ordinance and was later cleared by the Rajya Sabha.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes bills allowing extension of CBI and ED Directors' tenure up to five years
items.text: The Lok Sabha passed the Central Vigilance Commission (Amendment) Bill and the Delhi Special Police Establishment (Amendment) Bill, 2021, replacing the November ordinances and allowing yearly extensions of the ED and CBI Directors' two-year terms up to a total of five years. The Rajya Sabha cleared them shortly after.

items.headline: Rajya Sabha passes Surrogacy (Regulation) and Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Bills
items.text: The Rajya Sabha passed the Surrogacy (Regulation) Bill and the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Bill. The surrogacy law bans commercial surrogacy and permits only altruistic surrogacy, while the ART law sets up a national registry and regulation of fertility clinics and banks. Both were enacted during the Winter Session.
items.why: First statutory regulation of surrogacy and IVF clinics in India.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes bill clarifying when retired judges get additional pension
items.text: The Lok Sabha passed the High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, 2021, providing that additional pension becomes payable from the first day of the month in which a retired judge completes 80, 85, 90, 95 or 100 years. Law Minister Kiren Rijiju said the House was only clarifying legislative intent after contrary High Court rulings.

items.headline: Right against sexual harassment is part of right to life and dignity under Article 21 (Union of India v. Mudrika Singh)
items.text: In Union of India v. Mudrika Singh, the Supreme Court set aside a High Court order that had quashed disciplinary proceedings in a sexual harassment case on technical grounds, holding that the right against sexual harassment is part of the right to life and dignity under Article 21 and that service rules on workplace harassment must not be given a hyper-technical interpretation.
items.why: Strengthens workplace sexual harassment protections against procedural escape routes.

items.headline: Bill introduced to clarify additional pension for Supreme Court and High Court judges
items.text: The High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, 2021 was introduced in the Lok Sabha to clarify that retired judges become entitled to additional quantum of pension only on completing the specified age, overriding contrary High Court rulings.

items.headline: Parliament passes Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021 on first day of Winter Session
items.text: On the opening day of the Winter Session, both Houses passed the Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021 without debate, repealing the three agricultural laws enacted in September 2020 that had sparked a year-long farmers' protest and whose implementation the Supreme Court had stayed.

items.headline: BCI suspends 28 advocates accused of filing fake motor accident and compensation claims
items.text: The Bar Council of India informed the Supreme Court in Safiq Ahmed v. ICICI Lombard General Insurance that it had suspended 28 advocates accused of filing fake claims before Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals and under the Workmen Compensation Act in UP, and directed the UP Bar Council to finish disciplinary proceedings within three months.

items.headline: Supreme Court overturns Bombay HC 'skin-to-skin' POCSO ruling (Attorney General for India v. Satish)
items.text: In Attorney General for India v. Satish, a bench of Justices UU Lalit, S Ravindra Bhat and Bela M Trivedi set aside the Bombay High Court's view that groping a child over clothes is not 'sexual assault' under Section 7 of the POCSO Act, holding that sexual intent, not skin-to-skin contact, is the essential ingredient.
items.why: Restored the protective purpose of POCSO; the first appeal filed by the Attorney General in a criminal case.

items.headline: Centre notifies transfer of Madras HC Chief Justice Sanjib Banerjee to Meghalaya High Court
items.text: The Centre notified the transfer of Chief Justice Sanjib Banerjee from the Madras High Court to the Meghalaya High Court, as recommended by the Supreme Court Collegium on 16 September 2021, despite representations from over 200 advocates and the Madras Bar Association seeking reconsideration.
items.why: Renewed calls for transparency in Collegium transfer decisions.

items.headline: Ordinances allow extension of CBI and ED Directors' tenure up to five years
items.text: The President promulgated the Central Vigilance Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 and the Delhi Special Police Establishment (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021, allowing the tenure of the Directors of the Enforcement Directorate and the CBI to be extended by one year at a time beyond the fixed two-year term, up to a maximum of five years.
items.why: Challenged in the Supreme Court and later replaced by Acts of Parliament.

items.headline: Consortium of NLUs announces two CLATs in 2022: May 8 and December 18
items.text: The Consortium of National Law Universities decided to hold CLAT-2022 on 8 May 2022 and CLAT-2023 on 18 December 2022. Prof. Poonam Saxena (NLU Jodhpur) took over as Consortium President, and counselling fees were reduced from Rs 50,000 to Rs 30,000 for general category candidates.
items.why: Shifted the CLAT cycle to December, a change that continues.

items.headline: Pan-India Legal Awareness and Outreach Campaign concludes with valedictory ceremony
items.text: The 45-day NALSA-led Pan-India Legal Awareness and Outreach Campaign concluded with a valedictory ceremony, where speakers stressed that free legal aid is a matter of right and not charity.

items.headline: Collegium recommends Senior Advocate Saurabh Kirpal as Delhi High Court judge
items.text: The Supreme Court Collegium recommended Senior Advocate Saurabh Kirpal for appointment as a judge of the Delhi High Court, after his name had been deferred three times earlier. The decision was made public on 15 November 2021. If appointed he would be India's first openly gay High Court judge.
items.why: Put the issue of sexual orientation and judicial appointments at the centre of the Collegium-Centre debate.

items.headline: Law Ministry releases draft Mediation Bill, 2021 for public comments
items.text: The Department of Legal Affairs released a draft standalone Mediation Bill, 2021 providing for pre-litigation mediation, enforceable mediated settlement agreements, a Mediation Council of India, community mediation and registration of mediators, in line with India's commitments under the Singapore Convention on Mediation.
items.why: First step towards what became the Mediation Act, 2023.

items.headline: Bar Council of India conducts All India Bar Examination XVI on October 31
items.text: The Bar Council of India fixed 31 October 2021 as the date for AIBE-XVI, after extending the deadline for online applications to 25 September 2021. The examination, a prerequisite for law graduates to practise, had been deferred from its earlier March 2021 schedule due to the pandemic.

items.headline: Supreme Court orders independent expert probe into Pegasus spyware allegations (Manohar Lal Sharma v. Union of India)
items.text: In Manohar Lal Sharma v. Union of India (W.P.(Crl.) No. 314/2021), a bench led by CJI NV Ramana appointed a technical committee supervised by retired Justice R.V. Raveendran to examine whether Pegasus spyware was used against Indian citizens, holding that national security cannot be a ground for the State to get a free pass.
items.why: A landmark assertion of judicial review over state surveillance and the right to privacy.

items.headline: Centre notifies MTP (Amendment) Rules, 2021 allowing abortion up to 24 weeks for certain categories
items.text: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Rules, 2021 were notified to operationalise the 2021 amendment to the MTP Act. They specify the categories of women, such as survivors of sexual assault, minors and those with a change in marital status, eligible for termination between 20 and 24 weeks, and set up State-level Medical Boards.

items.headline: MHA extends BSF jurisdiction to 50 km from border in Punjab, West Bengal and Assam
items.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs modified the area in which the Border Security Force may exercise powers of search, seizure and arrest, raising it from 15 km to 50 km from the international border in Assam, Punjab and West Bengal and reducing it from 80 km to 50 km in Gujarat.
items.why: Triggered federalism objections and later litigation by Punjab.

items.headline: Centre notifies new Chief Justices for 8 High Courts and transfer of 5 Chief Justices
items.text: Acting on the Supreme Court Collegium's recommendations of 16 September 2021, the Centre notified the elevation of eight judges as Chief Justices (including Rajesh Bindal to Allahabad, Prakash Shrivastava to Calcutta and Satish Chandra Sharma to Telangana) and the transfer of five sitting Chief Justices, among them Akil Kureshi from Tripura to Rajasthan.
items.why: A single notification changed the leadership of 13 High Courts.

items.headline: Supreme Court lays down bail guidelines for accused not arrested during probe (Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI)
items.text: In Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI (LL 2021 SC 550), the Supreme Court issued guidelines for granting bail to accused persons who were not arrested during investigation and who appear on summons after the chargesheet is filed, categorising offences and cautioning against mechanical remand to custody.
items.why: Foundation of the later comprehensive Antil bail jurisprudence aimed at reducing unnecessary incarceration.

items.headline: Supreme Court takes up Lakhimpur Kheri violence, seeks UP status report on accused and arrests
items.text: A bench of CJI NV Ramana, Justices Surya Kant and Hima Kohli, hearing the suo motu case on the Lakhimpur Kheri violence in which eight people including four protesting farmers died, directed the Uttar Pradesh government to file a status report on the accused named in FIRs and whether they had been arrested.
items.why: Marked close Supreme Court monitoring of the probe into the killing of protesting farmers.

items.headline: NALSA launches 45-day Pan-India Legal Awareness and Outreach Campaign
items.text: A Pan-India Awareness and Outreach Campaign on legal rights and free legal aid was launched on 2 October 2021 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, as part of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav. Legal services authorities down to the taluk level were to run door-to-door awareness drives until 14 November 2021.
items.why: One of the largest legal-aid outreach exercises undertaken by the legal services institutions.
